entries.title: Adobe Acrobat will make editing PDFs in Gmail Google Drive easier
entries.summary: Google's partnership with Adobe will bring Adobe’s creative and productivity tools directly into the Google products you use every day. It will also bring Google’s frontier AI models into Adobe’s apps. The post Adobe Acrobat will make editing PDFs in Gmail Google Drive easier first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Adobe Acrobat is the best PDF viewer and editor, with tons of functionality. If you use Acrobat and Google products, there’s good news from the Adobe Max event. Adobe and Google have announced an expanded partnership that brings Adobe Acrobat directly into Gmail and Google Drive.

When previewing a PDF file in Google Drive or an attachment in Gmail, you will see a suggested “Edit with Acrobat” option. This creates a direct pathway to open, edit, and manage PDFs in Acrobat without needing to manually download the file first and upload it again. Adobe is expanding its connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise with Acrobat and additional creative tools. Adobe will also bring its creative tools to AI Mode in Google Search. Adobe and Google DeepMind will explore new editing capabilities for creative professionals, starting with an image model for Photoshop that could enable near-real-time edits.

Businesses will be able to use Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker agent in Gemini Enterprise — an AI assistant that helps teams design graphics, work with PDFs, and launch marketing campaigns without switching apps.

The companies noted that these integrations are coming soon, though specific rollout dates, regional availability, and subscription or account requirements have not yet been fully detailed.

entries.title: Audible will provide audiobooks for underrepresented youth
entries.summary: Audible launched Imagine Louder, a global social impact initiative that provides free six-month Audible Premium memberships to 15,000 young people. The post Audible will provide audiobooks for underrepresented youth first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible has announced it will partner with non-profits with its Imagine Louder campaign. At launch, the program will provide free six-month Audible Premium memberships to 15,000 young people within its first three years, offering more than 180,000 hours of listening per membership. Audible will work with seven nonprofit organizations serving underrepresented youth aged 12 to 18 in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Mexico in the first year, with plans to expand to additional marketplaces in subsequent years.

The seven nonprofits selected for the first year of the program include Girl Rising in Mexico; DreamYard, Flockworks, and Life Anew Restorative Justice in the U.S.; and VICTA, Be Free Campaign, and Exodus Youth Worx UK in the UK, with plans to expand to more countries in following years.

Audible piloted the program for six months to help refine how it could best support young people. Early results showed the positive impact of audio storytelling paired with dedicated programming: 77 percent of caregivers in Audible’s U.S. pilot with the nonprofit Reading Partners rated their child “engaged” or “very engaged” with audio content, 100 percent of teachers in the National Literacy Trust’s UK pilot agreed the program encouraged students to listen to more audiobooks, and 95 percent of Girl Rising participants in Mexico agreed that stories are a tool for self-expression and personal development.

“Ages 12 to 18 are the years when young people are figuring out who they are and what’s possible for their lives, and the stories they hear can shape how they see themselves and the world around them,” said Aisha Glover, Global Head of Urban Innovation at Audible. “Imagine Louder puts the power of audio storytelling directly into the hands of young people who don’t always have the same access and opportunity and gives the organizations we work with the tools to make that experience their own.”

Tiffany Jackson, Head of Social Innovation at Audible, emphasizes, “We wanted to ensure that we weren’t just providing access alone. These organizations know best how to leverage audiobooks in a way that helps the young people they work with reach their full potential.”

entries.title: First Look at the Kindle Paperwhite 2026 e-reader
entries.summary: Here is an unboxing and first look at the latest-generation Kindle Paperwhite 2026 model. Here are the hardware and software features you can expect when you buy one. The post First Look at the Kindle Paperwhite 2026 e-reader first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon has finally released the 13th-generation Kindle Paperwhite, and this e-reader should be enough for most people who love reading e-books and other digital content. The all-new Kindle Paperwhite is thinner and lighter than the previous lineup, waterproof, has adjustable warm light for comfortable reading at any hour, and offers up to 12 weeks of battery life on a single charge. The Paperwhite display uses an oxide-thin film transistor backplane and is the largest Kindle Paperwhite display with the highest contrast ratio—delivering deep blacks and crisp text, and images that pop off the screen, whether you’re reading in bright sunlight or under the covers at night.

The Kindle Paperwhite 2025 model features a 7-inch display with a resolution of 1264×1680 and 300 PPI E Ink Carta 1300. It includes an adjustable warm front light for comfortable day or night reading. Amazon redesigned the chassis to be thinner and lighter than the previous generation, measuring 6.9 by 5 by 0.27 inches (6.8 mm thick) and weighing 7.2 ounces (204 grams). The updated hardware relocates the power button to the top-right corner, adds a user-replaceable battery behind a removable back panel, and maintains an IPX8 waterproof rating.

Under the hood, the standard model ships with 16 GB of storage, Wi-Fi connectivity, and Bluetooth 5.1 support for Audible audiobooks. It charges via USB-C and delivers up to 12 weeks of battery life on a single charge. Upgrading to the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition increases storage to 32 GB, swaps the rear casing to aluminum, removes lock-screen ads, and adds an auto-adjusting front light. The Signature Edition also introduces a rotation sensor, double-tap page turns, and rear pogo pins for dock charging or attaching an optional magnetic page-turn cover.

New Software Additions for 2026

  • Ask This Book. Amazon rolled out a new AI tool that lets you query the text of your current book directly on the device.
  • Independent Mode Memory. The operating system now saves separate brightness levels for Light Mode and Dark Mode, automatically adjusting the screen when you switch themes.
  • Accessory Management Menu. A dedicated settings menu appears when accessories like the Kindle Click remote or magnetic page-turn cover are paired, showing accessory battery levels and letting you invert page-turn buttons.
  • Expanded Battery Monitoring. A new battery menu inside Device Options provides deeper visibility into power usage.

Core Reading & Interface Features

  • Navigation and Layouts. You can switch between cover grid or list views on the home screen, use multi-page previews while reading, and toggle page-turn animations.
  • Touchscreen Disable. Unlike the entry-level Kindle, the Paperwhite software lets you temporarily disable touch input to prevent accidental page turns.
  • Front Light Scheduling. You can set automated schedules for the warm front light to shift color temperature at sunset or on a custom timer.
  • Built-In Integrations. The three-dot menu houses Goodreads shelves, Amazon Kids, Family Sharing, a basic experimental web browser, and email export for book notes and highlights.
  • Accessibility and Audio. You can connect Bluetooth speakers or headphones to listen to Audible audiobooks or enable VoiceView text-to-speech across your library.

Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 16GB (newest model), Now thinner and lighter, 7" display, warm light...

  • The new Kindle Paperwhite: Thinner and lighter, with a high-contrast 7″ display. New edge-to-edge color, fast page turns, and a waterproof design.
  • Up to 12 weeks on a single charge: The display only uses power when you turn the page or use the front light.
  • Built to last with a replaceable battery: If the time comes, the back panel opens for a quick battery swap. Snap it back into place and keep reading.

entries.title: Barnes and Noble NOOK GlowLight 4 on sale for $99
entries.summary: The Barnes and Noble NOOK Glowlight 4 is on sale for $99.99; the regular price is $149, making it a good deal now that Kindle prices have dramatically increased. The post Barnes and Noble NOOK GlowLight 4 on sale for $99 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The standard NOOK GlowLight 4 typically retails for $149.99; however, the bookseller is running a limited-time sale, and you can buy one for $99.99. The deal is available to purchase on their website, but it can also be bought in all 650 of their retail stores in the United States.

The Barnes and Noble Nook Glowlight 4 features a 6-inch E INK Carta HD display with a resolution of 1072×1404 and 300 PPI. The screen is not flush with the bezel; instead, it is recessed. An all-new screen protector is installed at the factory to help protect the plastic e-paper display. This was a good move by B&N because it absorbs light rather than reflecting it like glass-based screens. When you read ebooks, the text looks crisper.

There are series of white and amber LED lights, so you can control the front-lit display and color temperature system. This will be customized with two slider bars in the settings menu. The front-lit display can only be tuned to automatically turn on at a specific time of day. It does not have an ambient light sensor; instead, it relies on the time of day. Physical page-turn buttons are on both sides of the screen, and they curl inward toward the back. The home button is at the bottom of the unit, marked with an N. Press it to return to the home screen; hold it for a couple of seconds to turn on the front-lit display.

Underneath the hood is an Allwinner B300 quad-core 1.5 GHZ CPU, 2GB of RAM, and 32GB of internal storage. You can charge the reader with a USB-C cable; this is the first time B&N has used a modern port on any of its E INK devices. It has Bluetooth 5.1 and WIFI 802.11 b/g/n to connect to the online bookstore to purchase and download ebooks. The bookseller sells audiobooks individually, but they also have a subscription program.

This e-reader is getting long in the tooth; it was released in 2021, making it the oldest e-reader still available for purchase. B&N disclosed that they will be releasing two new NOOK e-r-eaders sometime in 2027, but as of yet, there have been no FCC applications, so it will likely not come out until Spring or Summer.

entries.title: Rakuten Kobo released their 2026 Book Report
entries.summary: The Rakuten Kobo 2026 Book Report highlights a shift away from massive, one-size-fits-all blockbusters toward niche micro-communities, polar extremes, and sports-infused romance. The post Rakuten Kobo released their 2026 Book Report first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Kobo has released its annual Kobo Book Report, which provides an in-depth look at the reading habits, interests, and changing preferences of millions of readers globally. The year 2026 was notable for the popularity of book-to-screen adaptations, the appeal of cozy mysteries, and the allure of dark romance, spanning settings from the icy rinks of the Off Campus series to the stunning shores of Ithaca.

“This year marked a departure from the notion of ‘one book for everyone’ bestsellers, revealing what unfolds when fans connect with their communities. The intense enthusiasm for sports romance and a renewed interest in classics indicate that the traditional bestseller list is evolving,” stated Michael Tamblyn, CEO of Rakuten Kobo. “Readers are crafting their own reading experiences, discovering them in the diverse, vibrant spaces of the internet and social media. It’s become less about following trends and more about uncovering the narratives they didn’t realize they were anticipating.”

The Reading Trends That Defined 2026

BookTok has evolved. 2026 saw a shift away from singular viral titles toward dedicated sub-genres. Readers are finding their homes in niche book communities—from “sad girl lit” and cozy fantasy to specific romantasy sub-tropes.

The “Yin and Yang” of Reading

2026 was a year of contrasts. Readers balanced the high-stakes tension of dark romance with the comforting embrace of cozy mysteries. This duality extended to the bestseller lists, where classics like The Odyssey and Wuthering Heights butted up against newly-published favourites like The Calamity Club, Whistler, Land, London Falling and more. The breakout powerhouse of 2026 was Caro Claire Burke’s Yesteryear, launching a worldwide discourse around trad wives and trad lives. Whether it be the old or the new, the dark or the cozy, readers were in the mood for a bit of everything this year.

The “Hockey Boyfriend” Phenomenon

The sports romance craze—led by the Heated Rivalry and Off Campus series—dominated the charts in Canada, the U.S., Australia, Italy and Spain. It seems the world can’t get enough of love on ice and we don’t see this trend winding down anytime soon.

Page-to-screen Continues to Set the Scene:

From beloved classics like The Odyssey, Wuthering Heights and East of Eden, to crowd-pleasing contemporaries like Project Hail Mary, The Love Hypothesis, Verity and Sunrise on the Reaping, 2026 was chock-full of highly anticipated page-to-screen adaptations. The jury is still out on whether it’s best to read the book before or after watching; titles see interest spike around the time trailers drop and climb steadily until one to two months after official release. When it comes to influencing reading behaviour, it is undeniable page-to-screen reigns supreme, with adapted titles seeing a flock of new and re-readers, often reentering bestseller territory. 2026’s most-read page-to-screen adaptation? Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir.

The Changing Face of Romance

Contemporary romance darlings are branching out. Authors like Ali Hazelwood, Laurie Gilmore and B.K. Borison are successfully shifting their focus into the realm of magical realism, proving that romance readers are hungry for a touch of the ethereal. Meanwhile, through Kobo Writing Life we see indie authors continue to nurture niche genres before they hit the mainstream—including increasingly popular paranormal romance subgenres.

Regional Highlights: A Glance at Reading Around the Globe

  • The American Adaptations Engine: Movie and television adaptations are the primary drivers of book discovery in the U.S., with readers eager to engage with the source material behind their favorite scenes. Andy Weir’s Project Hail Mary clocked in as the bestselling title of the year thanks to the film adaptation’s major success at the box office. The Odyssey also saw a massive spike in sales around the time of release date, along with other popular Greek mythology retellings like Madeline Miller’s Circe and The Song of Achilles.
  • The Great Canadian Duality: Canadian readers are embracing the best of both worlds when it comes to literature. We’re seeing a real appetite for the sharp, jagged edges of psychological thrillers and dark romance, sitting beside a voracious hunger for ‘cozy’ reads that offer a safe place to land. We’d be remiss not to mention that patriotism is alive and well in the north, with hockey romance trailblazers Rachel Reid and Elle Kennedy dominating the bestseller list alongside contemporary cottage-country queen Carley Fortune.
  • Portugal’s Powerhouse: The Portuguese market continues to show incredible engagement with female voices. In 2026, nine out of the top 10 best-sellers were written by women.
  • The Dutch Lane: The Netherlands remains in a lane of its own, with a heavy preference for mystery and thriller titles. This year, it seems the Dutch are as eager to solve mysteries as they are to read them, as Murdoku was one of the most popular titles of the year.
  • Italian Identity: Italian readers continue to show a preference for stories set within their own borders, favoring narratives that reflect their own landscape, while also gravitating toward cozy reads as a direct response to the current global climate.
  • Freidamania: The influence of Frieda McFadden remained dominant across France, Portugal, and Spain throughout the year, proving that the appetite for gripping psychological tension knows no borders.

Looking Ahead: The 2027 Kobo Reading Forecast

As we look toward 2027, Kobo’s literary experts are tracking several emerging shifts:

  • The Folk Horror Boom: Expect a surge in “Folk Horror” reading in the new year, tapping into ancient anxieties and rural myths.
  • Dystopian Returns: As the global political and ecopolitical climate shifts, we anticipate a massive resurgence of dystopian and post-apocalyptic fiction.
  • The Trad Life Fascination: The “tradwife” movement has found a dark home in the fiction genre, as seen in the success of Yesteryear, and this fascination with domestic subversion is only expected to grow.
  • Genre-Blending Romantasy: Romantasy is evolving. We are seeing a move toward hybrid genres—romantasy mixed with political intrigue, myth retellings and complex mystery elements. Of course, we expect the Romantasy mainstays to continue dominating the genre, especially with new titles from Rebecca Yarros and Sarah J. Maas allowing readers to reenter the beloved worlds that kick-started the genre craze.

entries.title: E INK invests in Soofa, a provider of solar-powered digital information kiosks
entries.summary: Financial terms of the investment, including the amount invested and E Ink’s ownership stake in Soofa, were not disclosed. The post E INK invests in Soofa, a provider of solar-powered digital information kiosks first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E INK has just announced a strategic investment and partnership with Soofa, a provider of solar-powered digital information kiosks, to accelerate the deployment of sustainable outdoor signage across U.S. communities. The investment will support Soofa’s expansion and the adoption of E Ink’s 75-inch Kaleido Outdoor color ePaper displays, which are designed to deliver readable digital content in direct sunlight while consuming significantly less electricity than conventional digital signage.

Founded in 2014, Soofa develops solar-powered kiosks that display local news, public transportation updates, weather information, community announcements, and advertising in public spaces. The company has established relationships with more than 60 U.S. cities, including Boston, Atlanta, and Los Angeles. Its kiosks are designed to operate without connections to conventional electrical infrastructure, allowing municipalities, property owners, and advertisers to install digital information displays in locations where wired power may be difficult or expensive to provide.

Soofa’s kiosks are also designed for relatively straightforward installation. According to the companies, a two-person team can install the units without specialized equipment, reducing some of the logistical requirements associated with conventional digital signage.

“Soofa shows how E Ink technology can make useful information more accessible while keeping energy consumption low,” said Johnson Lee, chairman and CEO of E Ink.

“Our shared MIT Media Lab roots and longstanding collaboration make this investment especially meaningful. We are pleased to support Soofa’s next stage of growth and help bring sustainable community signage to more neighborhoods.”

The investment is part of E Ink’s broader strategy of supporting companies developing commercial applications for its display technology.

The Soofa transaction represents E Ink’s first investment in a company offering a complete digital signage solution, extending its involvement beyond display components into a business that combines hardware deployment, advertising operations and community relationships. The partnership brings together E Ink’s display development and manufacturing capabilities with Soofa’s experience operating public-facing advertising and information networks.

The investment positions Soofa to expand its solar-powered signage network while giving E Ink a more direct role in the growing market for low-power outdoor digital displays and community advertising infrastructure.

entries.title: Will you buy the new iPad Mini to read comics or books?
entries.summary: Would you buy the new Apple iPad Mini with an OLED screen to read books, comics, manga, magazines, or digital newspapers? The post Will you buy the new iPad Mini to read comics or books? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The newly released 8th-generation Apple iPad mini is powered by the A20 Pro chip and went on sale on November 6, 2026. This marks the most significant redesign in the device’s history, shifting to a stunning 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display while trimming its thickness to just 5.4 mm.

The 8th-generation iPad mini (2026) is a major leap forward for Apple’s smallest tablet, defined by its stunning 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display and ultra-thin 5.4 mm chassis. The shift to OLED completely transforms the visual experience, delivering deep contrast, 1,200 nits of peak HDR brightness, and a 24% reduction in bezel size that makes the hardware feel incredibly modern. Under the hood, the A20 Pro chip combined with 12GB of RAM turns this compact device into an absolute powerhouse, making multitasking fluid and driving local Apple Intelligence features with ease.

However, the redesign introduces a few bold engineering choices that serve as distinct trade-offs. To secure its new IP67 water and dust resistance rating, Apple eliminated physical speaker grilles entirely in favor of an Acoustic Display system that vibrates the screen to emit sound. While this projects audio directly toward the viewer, it can cause a noticeable physical vibration against your fingers at high volumes and lacks the acoustic depth of dedicated speaker ports. Furthermore, despite the premium price hike and the gorgeous OLED panel, the screen remains locked at a 60Hz refresh rate, which may disappoint users accustomed to the buttery-smooth scrolling of ProMotion on iPad Pro or iPhone Pro models.

If your primary use case is reading, investing an extra $150 for the matte nano-texture glass finish (available on the 256GB and 512GB tiers) is highly recommended. It scatters ambient light to drastically eliminate harsh reflections and mimics the glare-free properties of an E Ink e-reader, allowing you to comfortably read text outside or under bright overhead lights. Reading Comics, manga, magazines, newspapers, or e-books should provide a really good experience. Many app developers see the iPad as their flagship platform, so it gets lots of new features and enhancements before the Android version does. If you use the Kindle or Kobo app on the iPad, you can purchase digital content in the app.

Would you buy the new iPad Mini to read books and other content? The new device is more portable, weighs less and makes it easier to read on the go.

entries.title: Everything you want to know about Kobo Stack
entries.summary: Stack is the only option that makes a sideloaded book behave like a store-bought one, with progress and annotations syncing across devices. The post Everything you want to know about Kobo Stack first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Send to Kobo was officially announced last week, and the system is live on the Kobo Beta, currently available on their latest-generation e-readers. A Kobo Stack subscription is needed to take advantage of this feature. You can also use Send to Kobo by email, drag-and-drop e-book uploads on kobo.com, sync your uploaded books and annotations across devices, and use the extra journal and note-taking workbooks.

Here is how the Kobo Stack works. Email your e-books (PDF, EPUB, and LCP EPUB) and documents to your unique Kobo Stack address. They’ll instantly appear in your library on any connected device, such as e-readers or Kobo apps. Use the upload tool in the Kobo Cloud on the main Kobo website to drag and drop EPUB and PDF files. A subscription also supports Libby with multiple library cards, but the free tier allows this too. If you have a Libra Color, you can sync uploaded content & annotations across devices and use exclusive journaling and note-taking workbooks. The Kobo Clara BW does not include Google Drive or other cloud storage by default, but a subscription gives you access.

Kobo Stack subscription provides three years of worry-free reading. The extended manufacturer’s warranty offers comprehensive protection for your Kobo e-reader, instead of the default one-year warranty.

If you stop paying for the Kobo Stack subscription, you get a 60-day grace period. After that, the notes and annotations stored in Stack are permanently deleted, and so is anything else living only in the Stack cloud. Books already on your device stay, and so do your Kobo purchases. Kobo itself tells you to export your notes and download your files during those 60 days.

Stack needs the Kobo OS 6 beta, so for now it is limited to the Kobo Libra Colour, Kobo Clara Colour and Kobo Clara BW. The subscription costs around $3.99 USD per month, and the service costs around €2.99 per month. A free 90-day trial is available for beta participants. It remains to be seen whether the free trial will remain available once it rolls out to all Kobo users, or whether they will shorten the free subscription tier.

Some things you don’t need a Stack subscription for. You can use multiple library cards from Libby-supported libraries in your country. Users can load books onto their Kobo e-reader by simply using a USB cable. Calibre: great if you already keep a library on a computer. Wireless transfer is possible, but it requires your computer to be on and some setup. Dropbox or Google Drive access is still free for modern Kobo e-readers.

To subscribe to Stack, click this link and log in to your Kobo account with your username and password. The subscription uses your preferred payment method that is attached to your account and is charged every month after the trial ends.

entries.title: First Look at the Pocketbook INKPAD EO 2
entries.summary: The PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 is a premium 10.3-inch color e-note designed for reading, writing, and digital note-taking. The post First Look at the Pocketbook INKPAD EO 2 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 is a high-end, 10.3-inch color e-note and e-reader tablet running on Android 14. Launched in September, this second-generation device focuses heavily on productivity, combining a vibrant color display with an open app ecosystem and advanced handwriting recognition. However, it is still not available to be purchased yet on Amazon.

The PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 is a 10.3-inch color e-note tablet that features an E Ink Kaleido 3 display, offering a sharp 300 DPI for grayscale content (1860 x 2480) and 150 DPI for its 4,096-color mode (930 x 1240). Running on an open Android 14 operating system with full access to the Google Play Store, the device is powered by an octa-core MediaTek MT6765 processor clocked at 2.3GHz, paired with 4GB of RAM and 64GB of internal storage, which can be expanded via a microSD slot. To ensure visibility in any environment, it incorporates a SMARTlight frontlight system that lets users adjust both screen brightness and color temperature.

For productivity and multimedia, the 470-gram tablet has a large 4900 mAh battery and a proprietary active digital stylus (the PocketBook Stylus 2) for AI-powered handwriting recognition. Audio capabilities are highly integrated, featuring built-in stereo speakers and a quad-microphone array alongside Bluetooth 5.0 and Wi-Fi connectivity for seamless audiobook playback and voice recording. Physically, the device measures 191 x 225.6 x 7 mm, houses a USB-C port for charging and data transfer, and showcases a distinct, premium pinstriped backplate design.

Pocketbook’s strength is the number of supported e-book formats in its stock e-reading app. It supports AZW, AZW3, DOC, DOCX, EPUB, FB2, FB2.ZIP, HTM, HTML, MOBI, PDF, PRC, RTF, and TXT. Google Play will ensure you can install 3rd party apps on it, such as Libby, or Kindle.
